item.title: Beyond Individual Responsibility: A Qualitative Study of Capability, Motivation, and Opportunity for Self-Management in Early-Onset Type 2 Diabetes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study identified age-specific educational and support needs among individuals with early-onset type 2 diabetes. Optimal care requires multifaceted strategies, including person-centered coaching, provider training, age-specific education content, supportive services and environments, and tailored public health messaging, to promote self-management. Interdisciplinary collaboration is essential for implementation.

item.title: Comparison of the Safety and Efficacy of Remimazolam for Sedation in Adults Undergoing Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
item.description: CONCLUSION: Remimazolam provides effective sedation for fiberoptic bronchoscopy with advantages in terms of respiratory and hemodynamic safety, rapid recovery, and procedural efficiency.

item.description: FLOWERING LOCUS T (FT) functions as a florigen and plays a central role in the floral transition. item.title: Remote multicomponent intervention for older adults with cognitive impairment in community settings: multisite randomised controlled trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A remotely delivered multicomponent intervention improved cognition, functional independence and frailty in older adults with cognitive impairment identified through community-based screening. These findings support the effectiveness of scalable interventions integrated into community and primary care settings, particularly when access to in-person care is limited.

item.title: Long-term hepatic and extrahepatic outcomes in type 2 diabetes: final results of the prospective DM-FibroScan Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: LREs were relatively uncommon in the overall T2D population but increased substantially with advanced fibrosis. This study provides natural history data across the VCTE spectrum in a relatively unselected T2D cohort and supports integrating fibrosis assessment into routine T2D care.

item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that cyst(e)ine metabolism may represent a therapeutically relevant metabolic target for enhancing carboplatin response in ovarian cancer. item.title: Menopausal status modifies the association between migraine and cardiovascular disease risk: a nationwide cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Migraine was associated with increased CVD risk in women. Relative associations were stronger before menopause, whereas absolute excess incidence was greater after menopause. These findings highlight the importance of considering migraine in cardiovascular risk assessment across the female life course, including after menopause.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The results of this study suggest an association between subcutaneous mastectomy in adolescents with gynecomastia and favorable radiographic changes in cervical sagittal alignment. item.description: Nitrogen assimilation plays a crucial role in plant growth and protein accumulation. However, effect sizes vary substantially across studies [Hedges' g (hereinafter referred to as "g")=0.22 to 1.01], and a marked attenuation of treatment effects has been observed when translating findings from efficacy studies (g=0.59) to real-world effectiveness studies (g=0.30). item.description: With the 2025 revisions to the ISSCR Guidelines for Stem Cell Research and Clinical Translation, human stem cell-based embryo models (SCBEMs) sit within a clearer governance framework. We argue, however, that four practical challenges require further clarification. First, specialized oversight of human SCBEM research could be delayed where integration-building work is distributed across several protocols. item.title: Estimation of 24-hour urinary sodium excretion using spot urine sample in the adult population in shandong, china
item.description: This study assessed the reliability of equations for estimating 24-hour urinary sodium excretion using first-time morning urine samples. In this study, a total of 2078 residents of Shandong Province in 2019 and 2024 were randomised, and three equations for estimating 24-HUNa were fitted using morning urine samples and 24-hour urine samples from 1454 participants (46.6 ± 13.4 years old), and the three equations as well as equations developed by other researchers were validated. item.title: The Dissemination Research Logic Model for advancing dissemination science and practice
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The DRLM offers a flexible tool for visually depicting how dissemination processes unfold. The DRLM can strengthen the design, conduct, and reporting of dissemination studies while complementing broader approaches, such as knowledge mobilization. Future research should test and refine the DRLM across diverse projects and settings to increase conceptual clarity and comparability across studies and to accelerate dissemination science.

item.title: Design principles of prosthetic reconstruction after pelvic tumor resection: a systematic review and perspective from modular systems to 3D-printed personalized solutions
item.description: Pelvic reconstruction after tumor resection remains one of the greatest challenges in orthopaedic oncology because of the pelvis's complex anatomy, critical load-bearing function, and proximity to major neurovascular and visceral structures. Traditional reconstruction methods, including allografts and standardized modular prostheses, are limited by poor anatomical conformity, mechanical complications, and insufficient long-term stability. item.title: Deep learning and radiomics based on MRI predict recurrent lumbar disc herniation following percutaneous endoscopic lumbar discectomy
item.description: CONCLUSION: The radiomics-clinical model and CNN models showed good performance in predicting rLDH after PELD. These approaches can identify imaging features that may not be apparent on routine visual assessment. In clinical practice, the prediction results may help identify patients at increased risk of recurrence, facilitate preoperative counseling, and support closer postoperative follow-up and individualized rehabilitation strategies aimed at improving patient management.

item.title: Epidemiology and molecular evolution of Paslahepevirus balayani (Hepatitis E Virus) in fur-bearing animals in Hebei Province, China
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study systematically investigated HEV prevalence in fur-bearing animals and, for the first time, obtained the complete genome sequence of an HEV-4 isolate from mink in Hebei Province. This indicates that there may be a new subtype of HEV-4 in raccoon dogs, which provides the latest data of HEV infection and circulation in fur animals in Hebei Province and supports the formulation of effective public health policies.

item.title: Dimensions of implementation facilitation (IF): development of a tool for designing, documenting and reporting on IF strategies in healthcare settings
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The Implementation Facilitation Dimensions Worksheet provides guidance and a structured format intended to support the comprehensive design, documentation, and reporting of IF strategies. If the tool achieves its intended purpose, researchers and implementation practitioners may be better informed and equipped to make comparisons of IF strategies across studies and/or to replicate or spread successful IF strategies to other healthcare settings.

item.title: Salvage lateral open-wedge high tibial osteotomy for multiplanar deformity after failed cosmetic lateral closed-wedge high tibial osteotomy: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This case suggests that salvage LOWHTO may be a feasible joint-preserving option for complex multiplanar deformities after failed HTO.
